messages:
sara: Quick async check — where are we on the kernel contention patch that targets high batch sizes? Need a short ETA for the Friday milestone and an owner for canary + rollback plan. cc @mike @jordan

mike: I pushed the kernel lock adjustments to my branch (PR #4821). Running perf harness now. Preliminary: ~12% p95 token latency drop at batch=32 on llama-2-7b, memory +3% on worker VMs. No functional regressions in unit tests.

jordan: Re memory bump — do you know which change drove it? We saw something similar when jemalloc flags flipped during the allocator refactor.

mike: It's the async prefetch queue + bigger write buffer for KV. Short snippet: ```diff
- kv_prefetch_workers = 4
+ kv_prefetch_workers = 8  # improves throughput
```
That spawns slightly more buffers. If we drop workers to 6 memory looks closer to baseline but latency uplift is smaller.

ashley: I'll own the canary rollout. Proposed plan: staged on dev-region tonight — 10% nodes for 2h, verify spans, token-latency, and kv_evictions. Acceptance criteria: p95 improvement >= 5% and kv_evictions == 0. If evictions > 0 or error rate > 0.5%, revert.

deploy-bot: canary deployment started: runtime-canary/dev-region @ 2026-03-17T22:35:12Z (canary id: c-20260317-7)

lee: small ask for Private customers — please gate this behind a runtime flag so customers with strict memory caps don't see it by default.

mike: it's behind a flag already: `--kv_prefetch_async=true` and runtime config path `runtime.features.kernel_prefetch=async`. PR includes docs for toggling.

jordan: Dependency note: eng-sre will need updated alerts for kv_evictions and to relax downscale aggressiveness for canary clusters. Also we need an A/B trace tag so we can correlate p99 regressions to the feature. cc @nima

nima: on it. I'll add an alert: `kv_evictions > 0 for 5m` to be critical for canary namespace, and bump cluster downscale delay to 8m during the canary window. I'll also add a trace tag `experiment=async-prefetch` to the canary rollout.

ashley: thanks — mike, can you paste the simple rollback command so I have it in the runbook? Also attach the perf summary when you have it.

mike: Rollback steps (quick):
```
# turn feature off and restart canary
kubectl set env deployment/runtime KERNEL_PREFETCH=off -n runtime-canary
kubectl rollout restart deployment/runtime -n runtime-canary
```
Perf summary (dev-region lab run): p50 21ms -> 19ms, p95 120ms -> 105ms (12.5% drop), mem +3%. Test harness link: https://perf.internal/runs/4821

ashley: OK launching staged canary at 22:30 PT. I'll post status updates. Whoever sees kv_evictions > 0 please ping here immediately.

sara: thanks team — please keep replies minimal here unless you have an action. :thumbsup:

mike: quick note — if evictions appear but latency wins are strong we can try worker=6 as a middle ground. I'll open a follow-up PR for that knob.

ashley: noted — starting monitoring window. will call rollback if thresholds hit.

deploy-bot: canary health update @ 22:55 PT: 10% nodes healthy, spans OK, kv_evictions=0, token-latency p95 = 103ms (within expectations).

jordan: awesome. post-mortem/action items: 1) mike to land PR with feature flag and docs, 2) eng-sre (nima) to update alerts, 3) ashley to coordinate Dedicated/Private gating plan.

ashley: will file the short runbook and mark the milestone.

mike: PR link: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pull/4821 — moving to merge once canary holds for 4h.

sara: :thumbsup: thanks all.
